title: Pistons trade Isaiah Stewart to Grizzlies for 3 second-round picks: Source
content:
The Detroit Pistons have agreed to trade Isaiah Stewart, their longest-tenured player, to the Memphis Grizzlies for three second-round picks, according to league sources who were not authorized to speak publicly about the trade Wednesday.

The Pistons will receive a 2029 second-round pick that’s most favorable between Detroit, the New York Knicks and Milwaukee Bucks. They’ll also receive a 2031 Dallas Mavericks second-round pick in addition to their own second-round pick in 2032.

The move clears Stewart’s salary off the Pistons’ books. He is slated to make $15 million in each of the next two seasons, with the second a team option. Stewart, 25, averaged 10 points and five rebounds in 58 games last season. The Grizzlies will use a trade exception to absorb Stewart’s salary.

Detroit’s move to ship Stewart signals its belief in Paul Reed after he outplayed Jalen Duren and Stewart for the bulk of the postseason. Reed will assume the extra minutes Stewart leaves behind and step into a more prominent role as the primary backup big.

Look for the Pistons to continue exploring avenues to improve their roster in the coming days. The blockbuster trade between the Miami Heat and Bucks that sent Giannis Antetokounmpo and Bobby Portis to the Heat while rerouting Tyler Herro, Kel’el Ware, Jaime Jaquez Jr., Kasparas Jakučionis and five picks to the Bucks won’t be finalized until July 6.

Detroit could still be mulling over whether to get involved and expand the trade to acquire Herro.

Stewart was selected by the Portland Trail Blazers with the No. 16 pick in the 2020 NBA Draft, and Detroit traded for him after the draft. Stewart was well respected throughout the Pistons’ locker room and a fan favorite at Little Caesars Arena. His departure makes Cade Cunningham Detroit’s longest-tenured player.

ESPN was first to report the news.
